verdict.summary: Tensor::FromProto lacks a tensor_content length check before Helper<T>::Decode; an attacker can set N positive while tensor_content has fewer than N*sizeof(T) bytes, causing an out-of-bounds heap read during deserialization.

For DT_FLOAT, Decode reads sizeof(float)*N =  ㅤ bytes from a 1-byte content buffer, causing CWE-125. Helper<T>::Decode by standard semantics copies/decodes sizeof(T)*N bytes from content and has no visible in-fragment length guard
line4 validates shape syntax but does not relate shape num_elements to tensor_content length

The integer-overflow variant N*sizeof(T) in an unshown callee is not separately reported because no in-fragment cap or capacity demonstrates the overflow

limitations: TRACE_/PJ_LOG format arguments (e.g., %p used with non-pointer values) are not attacker-controlled format strings and are typically compiled out; not treated as findings.

The exact struct layouts of the RTCP XR report blocks are not shown, but the STATS struct is demonstrably larger than the 8 bytes available at the last word, which is sufficient to establish the OOB read.

verdict.summary: Compute() writes output_strides[output_shape.dims() - 1] without ensuring the input sparse tensors have rank >= 2. For attacker-supplied rank-1 shapes (truth_shape with a single element), group_dims is empty, output_shape becomes a 0-dim scalar, num_elements()==1 passes the OP_REQUIRES at L55-56, and the empty std::vector at L65 is written at index -1, a heap out-of-bounds write. Then group_dims is empty (L46), the L50-53 loop adds zero dims, output_elements==1 passes L55-56 (bystander guard constraining num_elements, not dims()), and output_strides has capacity output_shape.dims()==0 (L65). ValidateShapes (L15-18) and SparseTensor::Create (L35-37/L40-42) are unshown; per rules they are treated as opaque and provide no shown rejection of rank-1 inputs, which is why the rank-1 residual range stands.

verdict.summary: In CDATA parsing, the `while` loop looking for `]]>` uses `pj_scan_strcmp` as its only sentinel and lacks an EOF check. assumptions: `scanner` carries attacker-controlled XML bytes; the fragment imposes no length cap or EOF invariant on it.
`pj_scan_get_until_ch` leaves the cursor at EOF when its requested terminator is absent, as its name implies.
`pj_scan_strcmp` compares the current scan position and returns non-zero when the expected terminator is not present, including at EOF.
limitations: The PI and comment scanning loops show a similar missing-EOF pattern, but I did not elevate them to separate findings because their scanner-advancement behavior at EOF is not fully resolvable from this fragment alone.
The attribute-quote handling's `attr->value.slen -= 2` could underflow on malformed unterminated quoted attributes, but no shown consumer of that length is present, so it was demoted.
Recursive parse depth is unbounded for deeply nested valid XML, but depth control belongs to the caller and was not treated as the pair's one-statement fix.

verdict.summary: The CDATA scanning loop in xml_parse_node can fail to advance when a standalone ']' appears before the ']]>' delimiter, causing an infinite loop and CPU-exhaustion DoS on a valid attacker-controlled XML document.

No guard in the fragment constrains this; the absent one-statement fix is pj_scan_advance_n(scanner,1,PJ_FALSE);) inside the loop before the get_until_ch, which would skip the stray ']' and let the scan make progress (CWE-835 non-termination DoS).

assumptions: pj_scan_get_until_ch advances curptr only up to (not past) the stop character, so if curptr already sits on ']' it consumes nothing (behavior evidenced by the unbounded loop and consistent with PJLIB scanner semantics).

The scanner buffer is consumed via pj_scanner helpers that throw a syntax error when fewer than 3 bytes remain, so the non-termination witness needs only that the ']b]' position retains enough remaining bytes.
limitations: Unbounded recursion via the recursive xml_parse_node calls at lines  ​24,40,83 could also be a stack-exhaustion concern, but it is mitigated by PJ_CHECK_STACK() and was not the single-statement fix considered here; it is not reported as a separate confirmed finding.

The impact focuses on CPU/thread starvation remote DoS; severity is medium because it requires parsing an XML document with a CDATA section containing a lone ']' before the terminator.

verdict.summary: Integer overflow in the 'num_elements() * DataTypeSize(...)' product (lines 29-30) can wrap in unsigned 64-bit size_t arithmetic, making an enormously oversized constant tensor appear small and pass the '> max_constant_size_in_bytes' guard. The absent fix is the division-form comparison 'num_elements() > max_constant_size_in_bytes / DataTypeSize(...)' limitations: Exact upstream provenance (e.g. which CBOR fields produce these lengths) is not shown in the fragment; the overflow is nonetheless internally demonstrable because the unconstrained parameters are consumed directly at shown in-fragment memcpy sinks into a shown fixed-size buffer.

verdict.summary: In compile_xclass_matchingpath, the PT_CLIST property-kind check tests *cc (the property-type byte) instead of cc[-1] (the XCL_PROP/XCL_NOTPROP opcode), making it always false. For a PT_CLIST property marked XCL_PROP, the caseless-set characters are never folded into min/max; read_char then consumes the fallback 0..READ_CHAR_MAX range instead of the set bounds, generating an incorrect JIT range check for caseless property classes. The missing one-statement fix is replacing *cc == XCL_PROP with cc[-1] == XCL_PROP.

evidence.snippet: read_char(common, min, max, (unicode_status & XCLASS_NEEDS_UCD) ? backtracks : NULL,, 0);
evidence.reason: The attacker-reachable PT_CLIST property item with XCL_PROP takes the always-false guard at line   61 (which tests *cc instead of cc[-1] , wrong-target drift), rails through the else at lines    ️73-74 setting min=0,max=READ_CHAR_MAX, and reaches this read_char sink. The missing fix form (cc[-1] == XCL_PROP) would bound min/max tothe caseless set; without it the generated JIT range check uses the full range, yielding incorrect caseless-property matching. Primary mechanism: incorrect comparison (CWE-697) in the JIT compilation logic.

assumptions: cc is a parser-produced class bytecode body terminating at XCL_END; its property indices are treated as entry-point-derived because no in-fragment constraint bounds them.
read_char consumes min/max as the generated character range check, as implied by the shown call arguments and the surrounding generated-code comparisons.
limitations: The PRIV(ucd_boolprop_sets), PRIV(ucd_script_sets), PRIV(ucp_typerange), and PRIV(ucd_caseless_sets) accesses indexed by cc[1] have no declared capacities in the fragment, so no concrete out-of-bounds read can be confirmed for them.
No NULL dereference, injection, file/access, or crypto sink is demonstrable from the shown statements.
The finding is a logic/correctness flaw in the JIT generation path with no direct memory-safety impact, hence low severity.

verdict.summary: Unchecked positions indices from the attacker-controlled positions tensor are passed to optimized_ops::Gather, which uses them as offsets into input_data. An index that is negative or >= the gather-axis dimension causes an out-of-bounds read, because no bounds/validation statement constrains the positions values before the sink.

The absent one-statement fix is a runtime bounds check on each positions value (or propagation of the callee's failure), and the call's return status is also discarded before returning `kTfLiteOk` (line 10).

limitations: The exact numeric capacity (gather-axis dimension) is not spelled out as a literal invention the fragment, only via `GetTensorShape(input)`.
Any debug-only checks inside the callee (e.g., `TFLITE_DCHECK`) are not shown and cannot be relied on for release-build safety; the fragment itself provides no runtime guard.

verdict.summary: All buffer-index and length sinks in get_one_sourceline are protected by visible guards: the buflines index is bounds-checked at line24, the NUL store is capacity-checked at line28, and every buf[len-1]/buf[len-2] consumer is gated by the len>=1/len>=2 checks at lines45 and61; the only degenerate len==0 path (NUL-leading fgets input) is excluded before any sink.

verdict.summary: SQClass::NewSlot lacks an upper bound on cumulative class-member count. Once enough methods are inserted, the packed member marker created by _make_method_idx/_make_field_idx overflows its index/type bits; a method marker can then be misclassified by _isfield as a field, and the override slot _defaultvalues[_member_idx(temp)].val = val; writes out of bounds. The absent one-statement fix is a member-count cap (e.g., CountUsed() >= MEMBER_MAX_COUNT returning falsebefore insertion).

After the method count crosses the field-type bit boundary, a stored method marker is treated by _isfield at line8 as a field; at this sink _member_idx(temp) yields a low-bits index into _defaultvalues while that vector can be empty/small (only fields push to it at line46), so the write is out of bounds. No shown guard checks _member_idx(temp) against _defaultvalues.size(), and no count cap precedes marker creation at line34/45; the missing count-limit statement is the absent fix.

assumptions: key/val/bstatic are script-controlled entry-point data, allowing an attacker to force arbitrarily many distinct class-member insertions through this API.

The marker encoding implicated by _make_method_idx/_make_field_idx/_member_idx (lines 34,45,10,38) packs type bits and index into one integer with a finite-width index field; exceeding that width is what causes the field-bit misclassification and index truncation.
limitations: The exact 24-bit width and the MEMBER_MAX_COUNT constant are defined in the companion header, not in this fragment.
The concrete out-of-bounds witness requires an extremely large number of class members (tens of millions), so it is resource-intensive even though the CVE-2021-41556 root cause.
No vulnerability was confirmed for the other guards/sinks individually; `_metamethods[mmidx]` is considered bounded by the standard -1/valid-index contract of GetMetaMethodIdxByName.

verdict.summary: No security-relevant sink in the fragment is reached by a demonstrated failing value. The only memory operation is the unconditional `prog->type` dereference, but no NULL or invalid pointer producer is shown in the fragment, so it cannot be confirmed reachable.

No loops or array/container operations exist in the fragment, so no out-of-bounds, off-by-one, or iteration analysis applies.

verdict.summary: In the 'vertical' command-modifier case, checkforcmd_noparen() is called with &p instead of &eap->cmd, so eap->cmd is never advanced; any command beginning with 'vertical' triggers the same switch case forever via the loop's continue, causing reachable non-termination/DoS. The incorrect vim_isdigit(*eap->cmd) check at line  ️313 (likely intended *p) affects verbose-level parsing but has no confirmed security consumer in the shown code,and was not treated as a finding.

verdict.summary: In ReadTGAImage, an attacker-controlled TGA can set colormap_index and colormap_length both to zero (or colormap_index to zero for a colormap-type image), leaving image->colors==0; AcquireImageColormap(image,0,...) then provides no colormap storage, and the 8-bit decode path dereferences image->colormap[...] at the sink, causing a NULL/zero-size colormap dereference (out-of-bounds read/null pointer dereference).

AcquireImage at line56 returns a fresh image whose colormap pointer is initially NULL/size 0 when not subsequently allocated

verdict.summary: The raw image size `bh.width * bh.height * bh.bytes` is computed in 32-bit `guint32` arithmetic, so a maximum-size header (width=height=GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE, bytes=4) wraps the product to0/undersized before it is assigned to `gsize size`. The `G_MAXSIZE` sanitizer tests the product in 64-bit space and does not constrain the 32-bit computation (type/precision drift).. The undersized `brush_buf` is then consumed by `gimp_pixel_rgn_set_rect` asa full RGBA source, causing out-of-bounds read/NULL-derived read in the brush loader.

evidence.reason: All operands are guint32, so this expression wraps modulo 2^32 before assignment to gsize. With width=height=GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE and bytes=4 the product is2^32 and wraps to0;the G_MAXSIZE guard at line51 passes because it computes in64-bit gsize (drift class2) and does not constrain this arithmetic. The wrapped value is passed to g_mallocat line123, causing an undersized allocation later consumed as a full-width RGBA buffer at lines261-262. The absent fix is a gsize cast on one operand (or an equivalent gsize-domain overflow check before this computation.

The buffer `brush_buf` was allocated with the wrapped `size` from line122/123 (in the worst case zero-size, per the task’s `g_malloc` contract non-NULL, but zero-capacity). This call consumes `bh.width * bh.height * 4` bytes from it because the final image_type is RGBA, yielding an out-of-bounds heap read (CWE-125) from attacker-controlled dimensions. The same missing gsize-cast fix at line122 would have prevented the undersized allocation.

assumptions: GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE has itsstandard value 32768, which makes width=height=GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE, bytes=4 wrap exactly at2^32 in guint32 arithmetic.
Analysis assumes an LP64 build where gsize/G_MAXSIZE is64-bit,so the line51 check is type-drifted relative to the 32-bit size computation.
gimp_pixel_rgn_set_rect reads width*height*bpp bytes from the source buffer, per the API implied by its name and its width/height arguments.
limitations: If the `==240` checks at lines47-48 are taken literally, width/hheight==0 would also be admitted, causing divide-by-zero at line51; this is treated asa crash-only DoS/robustness limitation under the class-specific crash-only rule, not the primary finding.

The pattern-branch allocation at line165 has the same 32-bit wrap flaw; it is another manifestation of the same missing cast, but its reachability additionally depends on the earlier raw brush read succeeding, so it is not given a separate primary finding.

If GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE were smaller than32768, this exact wrap witness would not hold; the named GP constant is the value that the shown `> GIMP_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE` guard admits, and its standard value is32768.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the fixed counterpart of CVE-2022-30292-style thread_call: line  ight/6 reserves `nparams + 3` slots in the target thread stack before the `Push`/`sq_move` writes, covering the maximum `1 + (nparams-1)` pushed values and passing the Guard-Identity Audit on the same `nparams`/`SQInteger` value. verdict.summary: In the MBLOCK branch the ']' mark column is stored without any lower-bound clamp: `curbuf->b_op_end.col = bd.textcol + totlen - 1;`. With an empty yank line and `PUT_BLOCK_INNER` at cursor column 0, `totlen` and `bd.textcol` are both 0 so the expression evaluates to -1, which wraps into the unsigned `colnr_T` (`b_op_end.col`) as a huge invalid column that corrupts a persistent buffer position consumed by the PUT_CURSEND path and later buffer operations. The yank register may contain an empty line: the fragment itself special-cases `yanklen == 0` and `yanklen + spaces == 0` (lines 363 and 500),making an empty register line in-domain.

The two-pass '='-register split loop is self-consistent:the first pass counts without modifying (the write/NUL-replacement are guarded by `y_array != NULL`),andan identical second pass stores; `y_size` matches the allocation capacity.

NULL-deref and UAF candidates are covered by shown guards (lines 116-118,182,and 681-687;at least as far as this fragment can establish),and were not confirmed.

Internals of the unshown mb_head_off/curs_columns callees were not used to manufacture findings beyond the standard memory-read semantics of the pointer arguments supplied by the shown code.

The same missing minimum-length guard admits size values 1-3, for which the 4-byte memcmp at b reads past the malloc(size) allocation at line 11. This is a second instance of the same heap OOB read family; subsumed by the line-47 finding and by the absent 'size >= 12' check.

verdict.summary: Correct subject/object SID selection (parent's subjective SID for the subject, child/current's objective SID for the object) is present at line 4; no failing value reaches the avc_has_perm authorization decision.

The one-statement pair difference is not observable in isolation; no buggy counterpart (e.g., `task_sid(parent), current_sid(), ...)`) is present to contrast against.

mch_memmove(ptr, oldp + bd.textcol + delcount,
				(size_t)(oldlen - bd.textcol - delcount + 1));
evidence.reason: On the MBLOCK path the same negative-count failure is repeated: `count=-1` makes `totlen` negative (line371), `alloc(totlen + oldlen + 1)` (line372) can return a 1-byte buffer while `bd.textcol=0`, `delcount=0`, `oldlen=100`, and this memmove writes `oldlen+1` bytes, an independent heap out-of-bounds write from the same absent negative-count guard.

The separate `b_op_end.col` negative-mark issue (b_op_end.col = bd.textcol + totlen - 1) is treated as a correctness/robustness concern, not a confirmed in-fragment memory finding.

verdict.summary: esp_output_head's page-frag fast path calls skb_page_frag_refill with an unchecked ALIGN(tailen, L1_CACHE_BYTES) size, then registers/fills a tailen-byte page fragment; when tailen (or skb->data_len+tailen) exceeds PAGE_SIZE, refill can fall back toa single-order-0 page, causing an out-of-bounds write in the ESP output path.

The guard at line  iving only detects refill failure; no guard bounds tailen/allocsize (or skb->data_len+tailen) to that capacity before lines  iving‑52. The absent one-statement fix is an upper-bound fallback such as `if (ALIGN(skb->data_len + tailen, L1_CACHE_BYTES) > PAGE_SIZE) goto cow;` before line18.

Witness path needs `skb_cloned(skb)` false, `tailen > skb_tailroom(skb)`, `skb_shinfo(skb)->nr_frags < MAX_SKB_FRAGS`, and `!skb_has_frag_list(skb)` (lines18‑26), all satisfiable fromthe declared domains.
`skb_page_frag_refill` standard contract may return a base PAGE_SIZE page when larger high-order allocation fails/disables; so a true return does not guarantee enough room for `allocsize`.

Cow and tailroom paths are individually protected (line19; line74/82), so the finding is specific to the page-frag fast path.

verdict.summary: In the dyldcache dep-carving path, attacker-controlled depArray entries are used as an index into deps without any bound check (deps[dep_index]++), and the inner loop reads depArray[k] without k < depListCount, causing heap OOB write and OOB read.

With imagesCount=1 and depArray[k]=1, the sentinel test at line79 admits the value (1!=0xffff) and line81 writes deps[1] past the one-element heap allocation. The absent one-statement fix is a guard such as if (dep_index >= cache->hdr->imagesCount) continue;; before this write.

If the start index equals depListCount,or no 0xffff sentinel exists within the array,the condition reads past the allocation. The absent fix is adding k < depListCount to the loop condition.

verdict.summary: In ConstantFolding::IsSimplifiableReshape, the shape constant's dtype is validated only for DT_INT32; every other dtype falls into an else branch that reads the tensor as int64_t via flat<int64_t>(). limitations: If the library's flat<int64_t>() implementation itself performs a strict dtype CHECK before reading, the confirmed impact reduces to a reachable CHECK/DoS on malformed dtype, which is treated as fail-closed by the task rules.

verdict.summary: In --tls=require mode, an option rejected with NBD_REP_ERR_TLS_REQD is not payload-drained before 'continue'; the unread optlen bytes are then misread as the next option header, desynchronizing the handshake so that a subsequent NBD_OPT_STARTTLS cannot be processed and a MitM/early-payload attacker can prevent required TLS negotiation.

limitations: No memory-safety (OOB read/write, NULL deref) finding was confirmed; all visible buffer-indexed accesses in the INFO/GO and meta-context paths have explicit length guards.

verdict.summary: ELF parsing maps an attacker-controlled file and then uses unchecked ELF-header offsets/counts. The section-header table is derived from e_shoff without a bounds check and `shdr[e_shstrndx]` reads outside the file mapping; additionally `dynamic` is used uninitialized when no `.dynamic` section exists, enabling OOB reads/information disclosure on malformed ELF input.

An ELF with e_shnum==0 (or without that section) leaves it indeterminate, and it is then consumed as an index into `shdr`, an uninitialized read feeding a pointer/index sink. CWE-457 primary mechanism with possible OOB consequence. Absent fix: initialize `dynamic` (and `dynstr`) at declaration or check after the search loop.

verdict.summary: The conversion buffer szLineConv[1024] can be overrun: an attacker-controlled UTF-8/non-UTF8 line with 0xC3-style high bytes doubles output and reaches index 1024 unchecked (line 17/52); the UTF-16 byte-swap loop has no bound and can read/write past szLine when the line fills the buffer (line 69);and the terminator write after gf_utf8_wcstombs can write at index 1024 (line 78).

The while (1) swap loop (line 67) has no i bound;szLine capacity is lineSize (line 8). With lineSize==1024 anda file line of 1023 malformed UTF-16-like bytes (even positions non-zero, odd positions zero), no NUL pair exists in bounds; after i==1022 the loop reaches i==1024, and this condition reads szLine[1024]/szLine[1025] out of bounds (lines 70-72 may then write OOB).. The double-NUL break does not protect the full-buffer case. CWE-125 / CWE-787.

limitations: Frame-range guard at line 24 uses '>' rather than '>=' and is evaluated after the first gif->frames[frame] access at line 19; not confirmed because gif->frames capacity and frame_count_partial initialization are outside the fragment.

Physical OOB beyond 256 entries relies on the standard 256-entry table layout and 12-bit LZW acceptance documented in assumptions; the logical over-read (colour >= colour_table_size) is fully in-fragment.

verdict.summary: The temporary new_start buffer is allocated with alloc(), which leaves the heap memory uninitialized. limitations: A possible integer overflow in the needed_len computation is not relied upon; no in-fragment capacity bounds it, but the uninitialized-memory bug above is already determinable.

verdict.summary: The signed 32-bit complex-part lengths from get_st32 are stored in ut32; when -1 is supplied, n1/n2 become UINT32_MAX and n+1 wraps to 0. malloc(0) returns a usable pointer, and the ut32 truncation of rz_buf_read's st64 return lets the size check alias the wrapped length, so s1[n1] (and s2[n2]) perform an out-of-bounds heap write of one byte.

evidence.reason: n1 is attacker-controlled (line 16) and can be -1, stored as UINT32_MAX. malloc(n1 + 1) at line 22 wraps to activity, but malloc(0) can return non-NULL. rz_buf_read's st64 return is truncated into ut32 size (line 27), so an error return of -1 (or a 0xFFFFFFFF read count) makes size == n1 at line  ​28; the guard does not stop this path. The write at s1[n1] therefore hits index UINT32_MAX of a zero-capacity heap object, an OOB write; the absent fix is a UT32_ADD_OVFCHK(n1,1))-style overflow check before the allocation.

The same chain applies to n2: get_st32 (line 38) can yield UINT32_MAX, malloc(n2 + 1() at line 42 wraps to activity, the ut32 truncation of rz_buf_read's st64 return (line 47) lets the line  ​48 size check pass on error return -1 or a read of UINT32_MAX bytes, and s2[n2] writes out of bounds on the zero-sized allocation;the absent fix is a UT32_ADD_OVFCHK(n2,1)) overflow check.

malloc(0) returns a non-NULL unique pointer on the target libc/ASAN environment;otherwise the !s1 guard would exit before the sink.
limitations: A bytes-backed RzBuffer that returned only a short positive count (not -1() would cause the line  ​28 equality check to reject this witness; the exact buffer backend is not shown in the fragment, though the read API's documented -1 error result and io-backed read paths make the failure reachable.

verdict.summary: No attacker-reachable out-of-bounds, injection, crypto, or access-control failure is confirmed in the shown fragment; pixel-buffer allocation and read/decode bounds are covered by the MagickMax(..., columns+256UL) capacity margin and count/status checks.

verdict.summary: The surface-size calculation `width * height * 4ULL` overflows in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic before the `s > INT32_MAX` guard, so a wrapped small `s` reaches the allocation/surface path for a much larger `width`/`height`, producing an undersized surface buffer and causing out-of-bounds access in the subsequent surface/decoder usage.

For width=65536,height=65537, `width*height` wraps to65536 yielding s=262144, which passes `s > INT32_MAX` (line8) and reaches BufferPool_Take as the allocation size (line33) while the real size `(size_t)width*height*4` is 17180131328, so the surface buffer is undersized. The line8 guard tests the already-wrapped value, not the true size, and the absent one-statement fix is a pre-multiplication bound check or a widening cast on width before multiplication.

assumptions: UINT32 is a 32-bit unsigned type, so `width * height` is a 32-bit multiplication that wraps modulo 2^32.

verdict.summary: The fragment is the fixed form of SplashOutputDev::tilingPatternFill. The decisive protective statement is the guard at line 115 (`if (surface_width == 0 || surface_height == 0 || repeatX * repeatY <= 4) return false;`), which is evaluated after every assignment to surface_width/surface_height/repeatX/repeatY (lines 76-79, 91-103) and before all consumers (SplashBitmap allocation at line 123, result sizing at lines 165-166, the tile loops at lines 186-192, and drawImage at line 195). No failing value admitted by every guard reaches a sink with a memory-safety, injection, crypto, or authz consequence; remaining concerns (32-bit overflow of the repeatX*repeatY product permitting large-but-terminating tile loops, and implementation-defined NaN-to-int conversions feeding SplashBitmap) are DoS/robustness limitations whose impact depends on unshown callee semantics.

assumptions: `x0, y0, x1, y1, xStep, yStep, ptm, mat, bbox` are entry-point inputs parsed from the PDF pattern dictionary (full int/double domains, attacker-controlled); the only shown constraints are the equality check at lines 24-25 and the finiteness check on the composed CTM at lines 35-40.

`surface_width`/`surface_height` are produced only at lines 61-62, 76-77, 91-92 from `ceil(fabs(...))` of double values, so on ordinary (non-NaN) paths they are non-negative; the line-81 cap and the line-85-90 halving loop bound the product by 0x800000 and each dim by 16384 in the else branch.

`repeatX`/`repeatY` are produced only at lines 78-79 (tiny branch) and lines 94-103 (else branch) and are consumed unchanged at lines 108, 165-166, 186-192, and 195; line 115 is evaluated after all assignments and before all consumers, so it constrains the same int values, at the same type, at the control point the sinks read.

The allocation failure contract of `new SplashBitmap` (line 123) is evidenced in-fragment by the NULL check `bitmap->getDataPtr() == nullptr` at line 125, i.e., a failed allocation is handled before any use at lines 132-153.

`Splash::blitImage` (line 190) is assigned its standard semantics of clipping source/destination rectangles to the target bitmap, so out-of-range integer tile offsets are not treated as a memory-safety failure in this audit.
limitations: 32-bit overflow in the product `repeatX * repeatY` at line 115 (signed overflow is C UB; two's-complement targets wrap) can admit very large, non-overflowing repeat counts, e.g., x1-x0 = y1-y0 = 131073 admitted via lines 100-103 with the wrapped product 262449 > 4, producing a large but terminating tile loop at lines 186-192 (approximately 1.7e10 blitImage calls) — a resource-exhaustion/DoS concern (CWE-770), demoted because signed overflow is not a guaranteed wrap, the loop terminates, blitImage clips, and the resulting drawImage negative-dimension path (line 195) is unshown.

On NaN-producing paths (e.g., wid/ht == 0 or ptm rows == 0 cascading through 0/0 and 0*inf at lines 64-68), `(int)ceil(fabs(NaN))` is implementation-defined (INT_MIN on mainstream targets); negative dims could then reach `new SplashBitmap` at line 123 because line 115 tests `== 0` rather than `<= 0`. Impact (crash vs benign NULL from gmallocn) depends on unshown SplashBitmap/gmallocn internals, so this is a limitation, not a confirmed finding.

The integer divisions at lines 94-95 cannot be demonstrated to divide by exactly zero on a shown path: whenever a divisor would be 0 the preceding 0/0-NaN cascade makes it INT_MIN instead (lines 64-68 then 91-92), so no SIGFPE witness is derivable from the shown statements.

Lines 43-49 and 168-174 divide by ctm[1]/ctm[0]/matc[1]/matc[0] in double precision only (IEEE inf/NaN, not integer SIGFPE); the resulting non-finite values are at most passed to double computations or the shown guard set, not to a confirmed memory sink.
